segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[Page] 131. and it was proclaimed everywhere,
except among the Armeniacs, who did not submit on account of the oaths;
and the tyrant king killed them.
And in the year
{1108 OCR?} Harun al-Rashid passed through Edessa,
and the Muslims slandered the Christians,
saying: "The king of the Romans secretly comes every year and prays in their churches."
And when he investigated the matter
and found them to be liars,
the Muslims were driven away and even beaten.
At this time certain men of the family of the Gumaye in Edessa,
having squandered all their possessions,
dug in their houses and found a treasure.
And because they were profligate Arabs,
they indulged all the more in mounts and hunting dogs.
And when report of them reached King Harun,
he imprisoned them in Callinicus,
and sent his eunuch,
who took everything of the royal objects that they had bought.
There were among them objects like snakes and scorpions of silver, filled with coins {ksirin},
and through ignorance they had been scattered.
Then the eunuch seized their old mother and their noble wives,
and took from them whatever remained:
bowls of gold and silver, and miliaresia {milize}, heirlooms(?), and Roman dinars;
and he imprisoned them.
And their virgin sister he imprisoned in the house of a certain Chalcedonian, in an upper chamber above four stories,
and set Persians to guard her.
She, however, at night when she heard the sound of feet,
thought that one of the Persians was coming to violate her.
And she covered her face with a veil,
and threw herself from the window,
and died after a day.
And fear fell upon that eunuch,
and the king also was grieved on her account,
and he released her brothers,
and restored to them a fifth of their property.
And Mar Dionysius, because he was descended from the family of John of Rusafa,
was very knowledgeable about this affair.
And he says
that that house in which the treasure was found belonged to John,
and had been given in dowry of a daughter to the family of the Gumaye.
And the treasure, the wife of John had buried it,
when Khosrow ordered that she should go down into captivity.
Now King Constantine trampled upon the law and took a wife while his wife was living,
and he also used to take the daughters of the magnates and defile them.
